verdict: The initiative advanced 4 weighted points today to 68%. Tier 1 airport coverage and the 44-URL sitemap are live, but the score is capped by missing actual-cost reconciliation, assisted attribution, full Beacon funnel coverage and operating gates.

differences.before: Pages and sitemap ownership were split between legacy frontend and the new stack.
differences.now: Orbit owns a reviewed, eligibility-driven Bangalore inventory; legacy entries were removed and ALB routes one sitemap.
differences.why: Concentrate crawl and ranking authority instead of asking Google to reconcile duplicates.

differences.before: Pages could invent or silently change route identity, SEO fields and canonical URLs.
differences.now: Nexus owns canonical identities and content; Orbit protects search-critical contracts with executable tests.
differences.why: Make every route measurable and prevent routine UI changes from resetting SEO progress.

differences.before: Airport fare area, exact address, direction, terminal and flight details were conflated or lost.
differences.now: Each concept has a clear role and persists from search through quote, checkout and dispatch.
differences.why: Price against controlled geography while giving operations the exact trip information they need.

differences.before: Success was discussed through traffic, bookings or code shipped in isolation.
differences.now: Delivery, acquisition, funnel conversion, completed-trip economics and readiness gates are separate layers.
differences.why: Avoid scaling routes that attract traffic but fail operationally or lose money.

differences.before: Monitoring was an application concern with incomplete production ownership.
differences.now: Orbit emits bounded metrics, Terra owns collection and Beacon owns cross-system queries and alerts.
differences.why: Give every observability layer one accountable owner and make missing data visible rather than treating it as zero.
